scope: Later review advisories; original 120 assessments, hashes and human-review states remain unchanged.
approvalRule: A frozen reviewReady flag is historical. Apply the later advisory before deciding whether to approve that specific revision. No human approval is recorded.

records.title: An Efficacy Trial of an Intervention Program for Children Exposed to Intimate Partner Violence.

original.finding: ITT analyses found reduced internalizing problems for girls at follow-up; per-protocol analyses favored treatment for boys and girls immediately after treatment.
original.limitation: Benefits varied by analysis and sex; completer effects should not replace the more qualified ITT findings. Masking and attrition are not established here.
original.adverseFindings: Adverse events not established from accessed source; absence of reporting is not absence of harm.

records.newEvidence: The original 2015 paper, publicly posted by a coauthor, describes the first five eligible families at each site receiving intervention and the next five comparison. Authors call allocation random but do not describe a stochastic sequence or randomized starting rule. Its own methods are now accessible; the concern no longer rests solely on the later report.
records.revisedInterpretation: Randomization remains unverified pending reconciliation. Temporarily withhold the verified-RCT cross. This is not a definitive nonrandomized verdict. Original findings remain analysis- and sex-dependent.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: A contemporaneous protocol or allocation schedule must establish the random mechanism and reconcile five-family blocks here with six-family blocks in the follow-up. Do not approve the frozen revision meanwhile.
records.sourceLocation: Original Method / Study Protocol; later report pp. 853–854

records.title: Eight-year trajectories of behavior problems and resilience in children exposed to early-life intimate partner violence: The overlapping and distinct effects of individual factors, maternal characteristics, and early intervention.

original.finding: Long-term ITT analyses did not show significant intervention effects. Per-protocol participation in eight sessions was associated with fewer internalizing problems.
original.limitation: Only 68/120 attended long-term follow-up. The positive per-protocol association does not override the null randomized ITT result.
original.adverseFindings: Adverse events not established from accessed source; absence of reporting is not absence of harm.

records.newEvidence: The follow-up describes alternating six-family intervention/comparison blocks without a documented stochastic mechanism. Nine waitlist families crossed over and changed assignment was modeled. The fully adjusted post-hoc dose-by-time association lost significance after multiple-testing correction.
records.revisedInterpretation: Hold verified-randomization classification. Retain null treatment-by-time findings; qualify the reported ITT label and exploratory dose association. A complete longitudinal sample must not be replaced by the 68-person final-visit count.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: Reconcile the original allocation procedure, five-versus-six block descriptions and crossover analysis before approval of a new revision.
records.sourceLocation: Methods pp. 853–854; Table 5 and multiplicity discussion p. 858

records.title: Strength at Home Couples program to prevent military partner violence: A randomized controlled trial.

original.finding: Both partners reported less physical and psychological IPV; relationship satisfaction did not differ in exploratory analyses.
original.limitation: Cohort randomization and selected military couples limit transfer; prevention findings do not establish safety for coercive-control or high-danger couples.
original.adverseFindings: Not established from accessed abstract.

records.newEvidence: The newly accessed VA-hosted primary paper verifies cohort randomization and masked assessors. Figure 1 shows 138 people / 69 couples randomized; the registry records 156. Table 3 reports 12-month physical-IPV RR 0.53 (95% CI 0.25–1.12) for men and 0.43 (0.20–0.94) for women. The flow diagram does not resolve the registry difference.
records.revisedInterpretation: Do not read the broad frozen benefit statement as clear benefit in both partners. The male estimate remains compatible with no difference. Keep one RCT cross; neither registry DOUBLE nor assessor masking alone verifies two. Safety findings cannot be generalized to high-danger or coercive-control couples excluded or unrepresented by this selected prevention sample.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: Hold the frozen revision pending sample/registry reconciliation and a qualified replacement finding. Pilot inclusion is an unverified hypothesis, not an explanation.
records.sourceLocation: Figure 1 p. 937; allocation/masking p. 938; analysis p. 940; Tables 2–3 pp. 941–942

records.title: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial of the Strength at Home Men's Program for Partner Violence in Military Veterans.

original.finding: Strength at Home Men produced greater reductions in physical and psychological IPV than enhanced usual care through six months.
original.limitation: A veteran/service-member sample and referral comparator limit generalization; masking and attrition not established from abstract.
original.adverseFindings: Not established from accessed abstract.

records.newEvidence: Immediate physical recidivism was 23.3% versus 43.3% (p=.02); at the later assessment, about six months from baseline, it was 18.5% versus 26.7% (p=.30). Final physical-IPV Hedges g was 0.002 (95% CI −0.36 to 0.37).
records.revisedInterpretation: Modeled IPV trajectories favored treatment, but the immediate effect must not be presented as established comparative benefit on all outcomes through six months.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: Replace the broad durability claim in a separately hashed revision before approval. No additional source is required to make this wording correction.
records.sourceLocation: Results and Tables 2–4, pp. 1172–1174

records.title: Evaluation of an integrated intervention to reduce psychological distress and intimate partner violence in refugees: Results from the Nguvu cluster randomized feasibility trial.

original.finding: Some distress improvement was observed, but no sizeable IPV reduction; baseline imbalance and differential completion limit causal interpretation.
original.limitation: Feasibility cluster trial with imbalanced baseline characteristics and poorer applicability among women with severe IPV.
original.adverseFindings: Adverse-event reporting not established from accessed source; absence of reporting is not evidence of no harm.

records.newEvidence: Adjusted complete-case estimates did not establish clear distress or IPV benefit. An exploratory high-baseline-IPV subgroup had higher subsequent IPV frequency with Nguvu: mean difference 0.90 (95% CI 0.38–1.42). Three adverse events were judged unlikely related; one participant withdrew fearing neighbors would discover participation.
records.revisedInterpretation: Retain the null/uncertain comparative findings and the exploratory adverse-direction signal. Baseline imbalance, multiple testing and differential completion prevent attributing increased violence to treatment. Do not turn this signal into proof of caused harm.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: Add the qualified signal, actual adverse-event reporting and attrition limits to a new revision before approval; the available primary report supports this correction.
records.sourceLocation: Results sec020–sec022; Tables 4–5

records.title: Problem-solving therapy for pregnant women experiencing depressive symptoms and intimate partner violence: A randomised, controlled feasibility trial in rural Ethiopia.

original.finding: Recruitment and attendance were feasible, but allocation fidelity and provider communication needed improvement; this was not a powered efficacy trial.
original.limitation: Small feasibility trial; cultural interpretation of IPV impeded fidelity to randomization.
original.adverseFindings: Adverse-event reporting not established from accessed source; absence of reporting is not evidence of no harm.

records.newEvidence: Seventeen of 52 women were routed through a wrong allocation table and could not receive PST-IPV; only 35 entered the intended three-arm process. One serious adverse event was an assault by a participant’s husband; arm and causal attribution are unreported. Follow-up was missing for 13/52 and occurred early for 12/39 respondents.
records.revisedInterpretation: Treat this as feasibility learning with allocation and outcome-timing problems, not comparative efficacy. Report the assault without attributing it to the intervention or claiming absence of harm.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: Add the allocation deviation, assault and missing attribution to a new revision before approval. Arm-specific causal interpretation remains unavailable.
records.sourceLocation: Randomisation; Protocol deviations; Feasibility; Safety; Discussion

records.title: Screening and counselling in the primary care setting for women who have experienced intimate partner violence (WEAVE): a cluster randomised controlled trial.

original.finding: No benefit was detected for the primary quality-of-life, safety or general mental-health outcomes at 12 months. Depression caseness, a secondary outcome, was lower.
original.limitation: Patient and doctor masking was absent; 70–74% completed 12-month follow-up. A secondary depression result should not obscure null primary outcomes.
original.adverseFindings: Abstract reports no adverse events.

records.newEvidence: A same-trial harms abstract reports emotional distress and retraumatization from research participation. The 24-month report found no sustained secondary depression advantage. Neither supplies quantified excess harm caused by counselling.
records.revisedInterpretation: Keep the original null primary finding. Qualify “no adverse events” as the 2013 abstract’s report and include the related harms evidence separately. Do not conflate research-participation distress with proven treatment harm. Access to the 2013 report itself remains abstract-only.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: Amend the safety/durability context before approval. A legitimate full 2013 paper is still needed for direct appraisal of its own methods; companion evidence does not upgrade its access level.
records.sourceLocation: Harms-paper abstract; 24-month report Findings and Tables 3–4

records.title: Take a Breath, Break The Silence: The Effects of Yogic Breathing and Testimony About Battering on Feelings of Self-Efficacy in Battered Women

original.finding: Preliminary randomized evidence for combined breathing and testimony.
original.limitation: Only indexed primary abstract accessible; effect estimates, concealment and masking unresolved.
original.adverseFindings: Adverse-event reporting not established; absence of reporting is not evidence of safety.

records.newEvidence: The coauthor-deposited article describes a four-day experiment, selected self-efficacy findings, one missing combined-arm baseline and inconsistent statistical presentation. A referenced table was not exposed in the accessed text.
records.revisedInterpretation: Describe exploratory short-term findings only. Breathing-specific efficacy, synergy and durable benefit are not established. Withhold precise disputed estimates.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: Replace the broad preliminary-evidence statement with a qualified four-day interpretation before approval; exact disputed statistics require a readable facsimile or correction.
records.sourceLocation: Methods and Tables 1–5; referenced Table 6 not located

records.title: A Randomized Controlled Trial Comparing HOPE Treatment and Present-Centered Therapy in Women Residing in Shelter with PTSD from Intimate Partner Violence.

original.finding: Both active treatments showed substantial PTSD improvement and smaller improvements in violence, depression, empowerment and quality of life. The abstract does not establish HOPE superiority.
original.limitation: Both groups received active treatment; within-group improvement does not establish superiority or benefit against no treatment. Full methods and adverse-event reporting remain to be assessed.
original.adverseFindings: Adverse-event reporting not established from accessed source; absence of reporting is not evidence of no harm.

records.newEvidence: Full methods/results confirm no significant between-group outcome differences. At 12 months 127/172 were retained; ten needed different or higher care. The report states no study-related serious adverse events. Assessors were masked; participant masking is insufficiently explicit for two crosses.
records.revisedInterpretation: The frozen no-superiority interpretation remains appropriate. Narrow the adverse-event wording, add attrition, and retain one cross pending role-specific masking adjudication.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: No new hold on the conservative core finding. Review supplementary details in a new revision; do not award two crosses from the author’s double-blind label alone.
records.sourceLocation: Methods; retention/safety/results; Tables 2–4

records.title: Two-year follow up of a cluster randomised controlled trial for women experiencing intimate partner violence: effect of screening and family doctor-delivered counselling on quality of life, mental and physical health and abuse exposure.

original.finding: No 24-month benefit on quality of life, mental/physical health or IPV. The earlier secondary depression benefit was not maintained.
original.limitation: Only about 61% responded at 24 months; counselling uptake was 49%. Same trial as the 12-month WEAVE report.
original.adverseFindings: Adverse-event reporting not established from accessed source; absence of reporting is not evidence of no harm.

records.newEvidence: Full text confirms 166/272 follow-up responses and counselling uptake of 67/137. No 24-month comparative benefit was detected; the earlier secondary depression result did not persist.
records.revisedInterpretation: The frozen null/durability interpretation is confirmed. This is the same WEAVE cohort, not another independent trial.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: No new hold on the core finding. Human review of the fuller appraisal remains pending.
records.sourceLocation: Methods, Findings and Tables 3–4

records.title: Effects of mindfulness training on posttraumatic stress symptoms from a community-based pilot clinical trial among survivors of intimate partner violence.

original.finding: A null comparative pilot despite favourable within-group changes.
original.limitation: Small, unequal allocation; abstract-only appraisal.
original.adverseFindings: Adverse-event reporting not established; absence of reporting is not evidence of safety.

records.newEvidence: Full methods identify 29 randomized participants (19/10), unblinded assessors, unequal contact time and marked differential follow-up. The registry lists 35. A printed p-value conflicts with the narrative description of nonsignificance.
records.revisedInterpretation: Retain the null comparative pilot interpretation. Do not substitute favorable within-group change or resolve disputed statistics by inference.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: No new hold on the conservative null finding. Reconcile registry enrolment and statistical text before making stronger or precise quantitative claims.
records.sourceLocation: Methods, Results and registry outcomes/enrolment

records.title: Trauma-sensitive yoga as an adjunct mental health treatment in group therapy for survivors of domestic violence: a feasibility study.

original.finding: Feasibility evidence; efficacy and allocation method not established from abstract.
original.limitation: Very small controlled feasibility study with attrition.
original.adverseFindings: No harm reported by respondents; incomplete follow-up limits reassurance.

records.newEvidence: Full methods describe allocation according to availability into sequential groups, not verified randomization. Five of 17 participants were lost and the PTSD instrument changed.
records.revisedInterpretation: Retain feasibility-only interpretation and zero trial crosses. No efficacy conclusion follows from this very small nonrandom comparison.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: No new hold on the conservative finding; review the clarified allocation/measurement limitations.
records.sourceLocation: Methods and feasibility results

records.title: Using Mindfulness to Improve Mental Health Outcomes of Immigrant Women with Experiences of Intimate Partner Violence.

original.finding: Participant perspectives on a mindfulness component, without isolated efficacy evidence.
original.limitation: Small selected qualitative sample; multicomponent program.
original.adverseFindings: Adverse-event reporting not established; absence of reporting is not evidence of safety.

records.newEvidence: Full text identifies 18 selected English-speaking women from the intervention arm of a multicomponent parent study.
records.revisedInterpretation: Retain the qualitative interpretation and zero trial crosses. Parent-trial randomization does not make this selected qualitative report an RCT or isolate mindfulness efficacy.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: No new hold on the core finding; keep publication and study-family counts separate.
records.sourceLocation: Methods, sample selection and parent-study references

records.title: Child-parent psychotherapy: 6-month follow-up of a randomized controlled trial.

original.finding: Child behavior benefits persisted six months after treatment. Maternal distress benefits were present for completers but not significant in intention-to-treat analyses.
original.limitation: Follow-up of the original CPP trial, not an independent replication; differential completer and ITT findings temper maternal-effect claims.
original.adverseFindings: Adverse events not established from accessed source; absence of reporting is not absence of harm.

records.newEvidence: A primary reanalysis reports 52 follow-up participants while a program-author summary reports 50. The original 2006 full text remains inaccessible from the attempted route.
records.revisedInterpretation: The frozen distinction between child benefit and maternal completer-versus-ITT findings remains. Do not invent an exact analyzed denominator or treat a companion report as direct access to the 2006 methods.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: No new hold on the qualified abstract-level finding. Original flow/full methods are needed to reconcile the precise denominator.
records.sourceLocation: Reanalysis flow and program research summary

records.title: Examining strength at home couples to prevent intimate partner violence on a military installation: A randomized controlled trial.

original.finding: Effect-size patterns favored Strength at Home Couples for several IPV outcomes and suicidality; partner findings were less robust.
original.limitation: The abstract reports patterns without numerical estimates or intervals. Do not infer statistical significance for every outcome; selected military couples may differ from high-danger survivor settings.
original.adverseFindings: Not established from accessed abstract.

records.newEvidence: A plausibly related protocol plans ten pilot plus 140 trial couples. Registry enrolment is 150, while the publication reports 138 randomized couples. Achieved flow and exact paper linkage remain unverified.
records.revisedInterpretation: Retain the qualified abstract interpretation. The planned pilot is only a possible reconciliation; do not transfer planned masking, safety procedures or enrolment to the publication as observed facts.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: No new hold on the existing limited abstract finding. Full publication/registration linkage and achieved flow are required for added methods claims.
records.sourceLocation: Protocol pp. 1, 19–21; registry; publication abstract

records.title: Comparing Fathers for Change Individual Therapy for IPV Use to the Duluth Model Intervention in Individual and Group Formats.

original.finding: Individual-treatment participants attended more sessions, reported stronger alliances and less IPV; only Fathers for Change improved emotion regulation pre/post.
original.limitation: Pilot sample and self-reported outcomes. The emotion-regulation finding is within-group and does not by itself prove superiority.
original.adverseFindings: Not established from accessed abstract.

records.newEvidence: The paper and registry share grant R21HD099318. The protocol includes a planned 75-person three-arm phase and later two-arm phase; structured registry results describe 60/two arms, whereas the publication reports 82/three arms.
records.revisedInterpretation: Likely program-family linkage does not establish an exact results-population match. Do not transfer registry harms, attrition, null comparisons or masking into this paper.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: No new hold on the limited abstract interpretation. Phase/sample reconciliation is required for fuller registry-derived claims.
records.sourceLocation: Paper grant; protocol pp. 3, 7, 17; registry results

records.title: Psychological advocacy towards healing (PATH): A randomized controlled trial of a psychological intervention in a domestic violence service setting.

original.finding: Psychological advocacy modestly improved distress and depression at 12 months; anxiety and further abuse did not significantly improve.
original.limitation: 64% follow-up retention; open treatment and extra contact without an attention control. Imputation reduced effect estimates.
original.adverseFindings: 32 serious events in 22 women (15 intervention, seven control); four events had uncertain trial relation. Results and conclusion disagree about the arm for those four, so that attribution is unresolved.

records.newEvidence: The publisher Results place four events of uncertain trial relation in intervention participants, while the Conclusion places them in controls. Table 4 does not resolve attribution.
records.revisedInterpretation: The original source-check hold remains. Do not select an attribution from the inconsistent report.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: A primary correction or event-adjudication clarification is needed. No author contact is authorized or planned.
records.sourceLocation: Results, Conclusions and Table 4

records.title: The efficacy of narrative exposure therapy in a sample of Iranian women exposed to ongoing intimate partner violence-A randomized controlled trial.

original.finding: NET reduced PTSD, depression and perceived stress more than usual counselling. Functioning and further IPV did not differ significantly between groups.
original.limitation: Small trial; registry reports enrollment 34 versus 45 in publication and labels triple masking without execution details. Full-paper allocation, masking and attrition remain unverified.
original.adverseFindings: Adverse-event reporting not established from accessed source; absence of reporting is not evidence of no harm.

records.newEvidence: The paper reports 45 randomized women; the registry lists 34 actual participants and triple masking. No accessed source reconciles achieved enrolment or masking.
records.revisedInterpretation: The original hold remains. Do not assume that 34 means completers or that registered masking was implemented.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: A legitimately available full paper/flow diagram or primary registry update must reconcile enrolment and role-specific masking.
records.sourceLocation: Publication abstract; registry enrolment/masking

records.title: The effect of training problem-solving skills for pregnant women experiencing intimate partner violence: a randomized control trial.

original.finding: Post-treatment psychological and physical IPV prevalence favored training; sexual IPV did not. Allocation and cluster-analysis reporting limit confidence.
original.limitation: Only two health networks define arms; allocation wording is inconsistent and cluster adjustment is not established. Complete-case analysis and within-arm change tests need caution.
original.adverseFindings: Adverse-event reporting not established from accessed source; absence of reporting is not evidence of no harm.

records.newEvidence: Publisher methods repeat inconsistent quasi-experimental, network-level assignment and individual-randomization wording. The accessible sample flow does not identify the allocation unit.
records.revisedInterpretation: The original allocation hold and zero crosses remain.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: Contemporaneous allocation methods or a usable primary registration record are required; the attempted WHO route was inaccessible.
records.sourceLocation: Methods and sample flow; registration IRCT2013041713046N1

records.title: A randomized controlled trial of restorative justice-informed treatment for domestic violence crimes.

original.finding: The accessed original abstract reports lower new arrests and crime-severity scores for all offences over 24 months. Interpretation remains provisional until the linked publisher correction is resolved.
original.limitation: The headline outcomes include all offences, not only DV. Some standard restorative-justice elements were unattainable; effects cannot be generalized to unscreened conjoint processes. A linked publisher correction has not been substantively inspected.
original.adverseFindings: Not established from accessed abstract.

records.newEvidence: The linked correction is verified in metadata, but its substantive body remains unavailable. Its effect on the original report cannot be inferred.
records.revisedInterpretation: The original correction-related hold remains. Original outcomes cover all offences, not solely domestic violence.
records.requiredBeforeApproval: A legitimately accessible correction body, DOI 10.1038/s41562-019-0764-6, is needed before approval.
records.sourceLocation: Correction metadata only
